questions.question: ______ which translates to 'dance of the enchantress,' stands out as one of the most captivating expressions in the Indian classical dance repertoire.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohiniyattam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mohiniyattam** is a classical dance form from the Indian state of **Kerala** that translates to "dance of the enchantress."
 
• The dance is characterized by its **graceful movements, soft rhythms, and emotive expressions**, which are a hallmark of feminine charm.
 
• **Mohini** refers to a female enchantress in Indian mythology, and this dance form draws inspiration from the tale of Mohini, the female incarnation of Lord Vishnu.
 
• It combines elements of Kerala's two other classical dance forms, **Kathakali** and **Odissi**, and is performed to Carnatic music.
 
• The dance focuses on themes of **love, devotion, and spiritualism**, often depicting the stories of Hindu gods and goddesses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classical Dance Forms of India:**

 
 
• India is home to **eight classical dance forms**, including Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Odissi, Kuchipudi, Sattriya, Manipuri, and Mohiniyattam.
 
• Each dance form represents a unique cultural heritage and is recognized by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**, India’s national academy for performing arts.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music:**
 
 
• The music accompanying Mohiniyattam is Carnatic, a classical music form from South India.
 
• It emphasizes the use of traditional instruments such as the **mridangam, veena, and flute**.
 
 
 
• **Costume and Makeup:**
 
 
• The costume of Mohiniyattam is traditionally **white or off-white with golden borders**, symbolizing purity and elegance.
 
• The dancer wears **minimal jewelry** and emphasizes naturalistic expressions, called "lasya."
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:**
 
 
• Mohiniyattam, along with other Indian classical dances, has been recognized as an **Intangible Cultural Heritage** of humanity by UNESCO.

questions.question: What is the player who sits at the centre of the rectangular field in Kho Kho called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chaser**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the game of **Kho Kho**, the player who sits at the center of the rectangular field is called a **Chaser**.
 
• The Chaser's primary role is to chase and tag the **Defenders**, who try to avoid getting caught.
 
• The Chasers sit in a straight line at the center of the field, facing alternate directions, adhering to the rules of the game.
 
• The game involves a team of 12 players, out of which 9 players participate actively during chasing or defending phases.
 
• Kho Kho is a traditional Indian sport that emphasizes speed, agility, and teamwork, with the Chaser playing a pivotal role in the game.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Defender:**

 
 
• The **Defenders** are the players who try to avoid being tagged by the Chasers.
 
• They use their speed, agility, and strategic movements to evade the Chasers and maximize their time on the field.
 
 
 
• **Field Dimensions:**
 
 
• The standard size of a Kho Kho field is **29 meters long** and **16 meters wide**.
 
• The central lane, where the Chasers sit, divides the field into two halves.
 
 
 
• **Origins of Kho Kho:**
 
 
• Kho Kho originated in **India** and is considered one of the oldest traditional sports in the country.
 
• The game is believed to have evolved from a form of tag played in ancient times.
 
 
 
• **Key Rules:**
 
 
• Chasers can only change direction by crossing over the central line and passing through designated posts.
 
• The game is played in two innings, with teams alternating between Chasing and Defending.
 
 
 
• **International Recognition:**
 
 
• Kho Kho is governed internationally by the **Asian Kho Kho Federation** and is gaining popularity outside India, especially in South Asia.

questions.question: The Bara Imambara in Lucknow was built in the year 1784 by ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bara Imambara, also known as the Asafi Imambara, was built in **1784** by Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula, the fourth Nawab of Awadh.
 
• It was constructed during a devastating famine in the region to provide **employment to the local populace**.
 
• The structure is an excellent example of **Mughal architecture** with no use of iron or wood in its construction.
 
• The central hall of the Bara Imambara is one of the **largest arched constructions in the world**, measuring about 50 meters in length and 15 meters in height.
 
• The structure is also famous for the **Bhool Bhulaiya (labyrinth)**, a complex network of narrow corridors and staircases built on the upper floor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Architectural Significance:**

 
 
• The Bara Imambara is a unique blend of **Persian and Mughal architectural styles**.
 
• The entire structure was built without any supporting beams or iron, showcasing advanced engineering techniques of the era.
 
 
 
• **Historical Background:**
 
 
• Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula commissioned the project during a famine to provide **daily wages to laborers**, reflecting his commitment to public welfare.
 
• The construction employed thousands of workers, both skilled and unskilled, as a famine relief measure.
 
 
 
• **Bhool Bhulaiya:**
 
 
• The labyrinth is a network of interconnected passages designed to confuse intruders and also served as a strategic defense mechanism.
 
• It is a major tourist attraction and adds a mysterious charm to the structure.
 
 
 
• **Religious Significance:**
 
 
• The Bara Imambara is an important religious site for **Shia Muslims**, as it serves as a congregation hall for religious ceremonies, particularly during the month of Muharram.

questions.question: Which of the following states in India had the LOWEST poverty ratio in 2011-2012 as per the Economic Survey 2013-14, released by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the Economic Survey 2013-14, Kerala recorded the **lowest poverty ratio** in India for the year 2011-2012.
 
• The poverty ratio in Kerala was significantly low at **7.05%**, as per the data.
 
• This achievement is attributed to Kerala's high literacy rates, progressive social reforms, and effective social welfare programs.
 
• Kerala has consistently prioritized investments in health, education, and social security, which have contributed to poverty alleviation.
 
• States like Bihar, Odisha, and Madhya Pradesh, in contrast, had much higher poverty ratios during the same period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Poverty Ratio:**

 
 
• The poverty ratio is the percentage of the population living below the poverty line, which is based on income and consumption levels.
 
• In India, the poverty line is determined using the Tendulkar Methodology, which considers monthly per capita consumption expenditure.
 
 
 
• **Kerala's Model of Development:**
 
 
• Kerala’s development model focuses on human development indicators such as literacy, healthcare, and life expectancy.
 
• It has achieved near-universal literacy and one of the highest Human Development Index (HDI) scores in India.
 
 
 
• **Economic Survey:**
 
 
• The Economic Survey is an annual document released by the Ministry of Finance, reviewing the economy's performance over the past year.
 
• It provides data on key economic indicators, including poverty, growth, inflation, and fiscal performance.
 
 
 
• **Poverty Alleviation Schemes:**
 
 
• India has implemented several poverty alleviation schemes, such as MGNREGA, PMAY (Housing for All), and NFSA (Food Security).
 
• These schemes aim to provide employment, housing, and food security to reduce poverty.

questions.question: How much amount is provided per month as assistance to the female head of the family under the Gruha Lakshmi Scheme launched by the Karnataka Government in July 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹2,000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Karnataka Government launched the **Gruha Lakshmi Scheme** in July 2023 to provide financial assistance to women heading households.
 
• Under this scheme, ₹2,000 per month is provided to the **female head of the family** as direct financial aid.
 
• The scheme aims to empower women and enhance their **socio-economic status** by offering financial independence.
 
• This initiative is expected to benefit approximately **1.28 crore women** across the state.
 
• The **direct benefit transfer (DBT)** mechanism is used to ensure transparency and efficient delivery of funds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gruha Lakshmi Scheme:**

 
 
• This scheme focuses on **women empowerment** by providing financial aid to support household expenses.
 
• It aligns with the state government’s broader agenda of **social welfare and poverty alleviation**.
 
 
 
• **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT):**
 
 
• DBT is a method of transferring subsidies or benefits directly to the beneficiaries' bank accounts, eliminating intermediaries.
 
• It ensures greater transparency and reduces leakages in fund distribution.
 
 
 
• **Other Karnataka Schemes:**
 
 
• **Gruha Jyothi Scheme:** Provides free electricity up to 200 units per month to households.
 
• **Anna Bhagya Scheme:** Offers free rice to families below the poverty line.
 
 
 
• **Women Empowerment in India:**
 
 
• Various state and central government schemes aim to promote gender equality and financial independence for women.
 
• Empowering women contributes to overall economic growth and societal development.

questions.question: Who among the following is the author of the famous novel, 'One Amazing Thing'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni is an Indian-American author known for her novels that explore themes like immigration, identity, and cultural dissonance.
 
• 'One Amazing Thing' is one of her critically acclaimed novels, which revolves around diverse characters trapped together during a disaster.
 
• Her writing often focuses on the experiences of South Asian immigrants, blending literary and cultural elements.
 
• Divakaruni's works have received several awards, including the American Book Award and the Light of India Award for Excellence in Literature.
 
• She is also known for other notable works such as 'The Mistress of Spices,' 'Sister of My Heart,' and 'Palace of Illusions.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Immigration Themes in Literature:**

 
 
• Explores the struggles of adapting to new cultures and maintaining one's identity in a foreign land.
 
• Often incorporates themes of nostalgia, loss, and resilience.
 
 
 
• **Literary Style of Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni:**
 
 
• Known for blending magical realism with traditional storytelling.
 
• Her works often highlight the complexities of human relationships and the interconnectedness of lives.
 
 
 
• **Representation of South Asian Culture:**
 
 
• Divakaruni's novels frequently portray South Asian traditions, family dynamics, and societal norms.
 
• Her works serve as a bridge to introduce South Asian culture to a global audience.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable South Asian Authors:**
 
 
• Amitav Ghosh – Known for 'The Shadow Lines' and 'Sea of Poppies.'
 
• Jhumpa Lahiri – Famous for 'Interpreter of Maladies' and 'The Namesake.'

questions.question: Which of the following is the national fruit of Sri Lanka?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jackfruit**__.

*__Key Points__

__
 
• The national fruit of Sri Lanka is **Jackfruit**, known for its distinctive flavor and large size.
 
• Jackfruit is widely cultivated in Sri Lanka and is a staple ingredient in many traditional dishes.
 
• It is considered one of the largest tree-borne fruits globally, with some specimens weighing up to 40 kilograms.
 
• In Sri Lankan cuisine, jackfruit is utilized in various forms, including raw as a vegetable (e.g., "Polos Curry") and ripe as a sweet fruit.
 
• Jackfruit trees contribute significantly to local agriculture and livelihoods, being valued for their wood, fruit, and overall sustainability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scientific Name:** The scientific name of jackfruit is Artocarpus heterophyllus*.
 
• **Health Benefits:** Jackfruit is rich in dietary fiber, vitamins (like vitamin C), and minerals, making it highly nutritious.
 
• **Ecological Importance:** Jackfruit trees are drought-resistant and adaptable to tropical climates, contributing to sustainable agriculture.
 
• **Cultural Significance:** In many South Asian cultures, jackfruit is considered a symbol of abundance and prosperity.
 
• **Global Popularity:** While native to South and Southeast Asia, jackfruit has gained popularity worldwide due to its versatility, including being used as a vegan meat substitute.

questions.question: In which the following sports do caddies play the role of helper for the player?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Golf**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **caddie** is an individual who assists a golfer during a game by carrying their golf bag, clubs, and providing advice.
 
• Caddies play an essential role in **strategy and decision-making** during a golf game, offering insights on club selection, reading greens, and understanding course layouts.
 
• The relationship between a golfer and their caddie is often critical to the golfer's performance, especially in competitive tournaments.
 
• Caddies are commonly seen in professional golf tournaments, such as those organized by **PGA Tour** and **LPGA Tour**.
 
• While golf is the primary sport where caddies are involved, they are not present in sports like cycling, boxing, shooting, or others listed in the question.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Origin of Caddies:**

 
 
• The term "caddie" is derived from the French word "**cadet**," meaning "young assistant" or "trainee."
 
• It was popularized in golf by Mary, Queen of Scots, who brought the concept of cadets to carry clubs in the 16th century.
 
 
 
• **Responsibilities of a Caddie:**
 
 
• Carrying the golfer's bag and equipment throughout the course.
 
• Providing insights on distance, wind direction, and course conditions.
 
• Assisting with rules and etiquette during the game.
 
 
 
• **Famous Caddie-Golfer Partnerships:**
 
 
• **Steve Williams** and Tiger Woods: Steve worked as Tiger Woods' caddie for over a decade, contributing to many of his major wins.
 
• **Jim "Bones" Mackay** and Phil Mickelson: Their partnership is regarded as one of the most successful in golf history.
 
 
 
• **Modern Caddie Systems:**
 
 
• In amateur golf, players often use **trolleys** or **golf carts** instead of caddies.
 
• Professional tournaments still mandate caddies to ensure players have strategic support.

questions.question: Who among the following Mughal emperors had a great interest in paintings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jahangir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Jahangir**, the Mughal emperor (1605–1627), was a patron of the arts, particularly known for his profound interest in paintings and miniature art.
 
• He established a **royal atelier** where skilled painters like Mansur and Abul Hasan flourished under his patronage.
 
• Jahangir is celebrated for introducing **naturalism** in Mughal paintings, with a focus on lifelike portrayals of flora, fauna, and portraits.
 
• He personally reviewed paintings and showed a keen interest in their details, often rewarding artists for their exceptional work.
 
• The period of Jahangir's rule is considered the **golden age of Mughal painting**, marked by the creation of masterpieces like the "Jahangirnama" illustrations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mughal Miniature Paintings:**

 
 
• Miniature painting is a style of art that flourished under the Mughal Empire, combining Persian, Indian, and European influences.
 
• It emphasized intricate details, vibrant colors, and elaborate compositions.
 
• Popular themes included court life, battles, nature, and portraits.
 
 
 
• **Jahangirnama:**
 
 
• The "Jahangirnama" is the autobiography of Jahangir, detailing his life and reign.
 
• It contains vivid descriptions of his love for art, nature, and justice.
 
• The manuscript is richly illustrated with paintings that showcase the artistic achievements of his time.
 
 
 
• **Ustad Mansur:**
 
 
• One of the most famous painters in Jahangir's court, known for his exceptional depictions of animals and plants.
 
• He was titled "Nadir-al-Asr" (Wonder of the Age) by Jahangir for his naturalistic works.
 
 
 
• **Naturalism in Mughal Art:**
 
 
• Introduced by Jahangir, this style focused on realistic and lifelike depictions of subjects.
 
• It marked a departure from the heavily stylized art of earlier periods, emphasizing close observation of nature.

questions.question: Chhath Puja falls in which month of the Hindu calendar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kartika**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chhath Puja** is celebrated in the month of **Kartika** (October-November) as per the Hindu calendar, specifically on the sixth day after Diwali.
 
• It is a major festival in **Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh,** and parts of Nepal, observed to honor the **Sun God (Surya Dev)** and his consort **Chhathi Maiya**.
 
• The festival spans **four days** and includes rituals like fasting, holy bathing in rivers, and offering Arghya (water offering) to the setting and rising sun.
 
• Chhath Puja is known for its emphasis on **purity, devotion, and environmental harmony**.
 
• The main rituals are conducted along riverbanks, with devotees preparing offerings such as **thekua, fruits, and sugarcane**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Significance of Chhath Puja**:

 
 
• The festival is dedicated to **Surya Dev (Sun God)**, who is considered the source of life and energy.
 
• It is believed to bring prosperity, health, and well-being to devotees and their families.
 
 
 
• **Chhathi Maiya**:
 
 
• Chhathi Maiya is worshipped as the **goddess of fertility and health**.
 
• She is believed to bless families with happiness and offspring.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Aspect**:
 
 
• Chhath Puja promotes **cleanliness and eco-friendly practices**, as devotees clean riverbanks and avoid using synthetic materials.
 
• The offerings are biodegradable, emphasizing environmental sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Four-Day Ritual Breakdown**:
 
 
• Day 1: **Nahay Khay** – Devotees clean their homes and prepare for fasting.
 
• Day 2: **Kharna** – A day-long fast is broken with a simple meal, followed by a 36-hour nirjala (waterless) fast.
 
• Day 3: **Sandhya Arghya** – Offerings are made to the setting sun at riverbanks.
 
• Day 4: **Usha Arghya** – Rituals conclude with offerings to the rising sun.
 
 
 
• **Origins and Historical Context**:
 
 
• The festival traces its roots to ancient Vedic rituals, where the Sun God was revered as a sustainer of life.
 
• It is mentioned in texts like the Rigveda, highlighting the importance of solar worship.

questions.question: What is the salt measurement in hypersaline lagoons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**More than 100**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Hypersaline lagoons** are characterized by extremely high salinity levels, often exceeding **100 ppt (parts per thousand)**.
 
• These salinity levels occur due to **intense evaporation rates** and limited water exchange with open seas or freshwater sources.
 
• Such lagoons are typically found in **arid or semi-arid regions** where evaporation surpasses precipitation.
 
• Examples of hypersaline lagoons include **Laguna Madre (Texas, USA)** and various lagoons in the Middle East and Australia.
 
• The high salinity environment supports **specialized organisms** such as halophilic bacteria and algae, adapted to thrive in extreme conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salinity Measurement:**

 
 
• Salinity is usually measured in **parts per thousand (ppt)**, representing the amount of dissolved salts in water.
 
• Normal seawater salinity is approximately **35 ppt**, whereas hypersaline environments exceed **100 ppt**.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation and Salinity:**
 
 
• **Evaporation** is a key factor in hypersaline lagoons, significantly increasing salinity by removing water and concentrating salts.
 
• The absence of significant freshwater input further exacerbates salinity levels.
 
 
 
• **Halophiles:**
 
 
• Organisms such as **halophilic bacteria and archaea** are specially adapted to survive in high-salinity environments.
 
• These organisms play essential roles in nutrient cycles within hypersaline ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance:**
 
 
• Hypersaline lagoons are unique ecosystems, providing habitats for specialized species.
 
• They act as natural laboratories for studying **extremophile organisms** and their adaptations.

questions.question: Name the Sri Lankan Buddhist text that provides details of the Mauryan empire.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dipavamsa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dipavamsa** is an ancient Buddhist chronicle written in the **Pali language** in Sri Lanka.
 
• It is considered the **earliest extant historical record** of Sri Lanka, dating back to the 3rd-4th century CE.
 
• The text provides valuable insights into the **history of the Mauryan Empire**, particularly Emperor Ashoka's role in spreading Buddhism.
 
• It documents the arrival of Buddhism in Sri Lanka, including the **mission of Mahinda**, Emperor Ashoka's son, who introduced Buddhism to the island.
 
• Dipavamsa served as a precursor to the later and more detailed Sri Lankan chronicle, the **Mahavamsa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahavamsa:**

 
 
• The **Mahavamsa** is another significant Buddhist chronicle of Sri Lanka written in Pali, continuing the historical record found in the Dipavamsa.
 
• It provides a more detailed and structured account of Sri Lankan history and Buddhism compared to the Dipavamsa.
 
 
 
• **Buddhist Texts:**
 
 
• The **Ashokavadana** is a Buddhist text that narrates the life and deeds of Emperor Ashoka but is not specific to Sri Lankan history.
 
• The **Divyavadana** is a collection of Buddhist legends, also focusing on Ashoka and his contributions to Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Emperor Ashoka:**
 
 
• Ashoka was a Mauryan emperor who played a pivotal role in the spread of Buddhism in India and beyond.
 
• His son, Mahinda, and daughter, Sanghamitta, are credited with propagating Buddhism in Sri Lanka.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Dipavamsa:**
 
 
• Dipavamsa serves as an essential source for understanding the cultural and religious history of ancient Sri Lanka.
 
• It highlights the impact of Indian influence, particularly through the Mauryan Empire, on Sri Lankan society and religion.

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: Shree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam (SNDP), founded in 1903, to carry on the work of social reform was active in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam (SNDP)** was founded in 1903 by **Sree Narayana Guru**, a social reformer and spiritual leader from Kerala.
 
• The organization was established to work for the **upliftment of the Ezhava community**, a marginalized group in Kerala, and to promote social equality and education.
 
• SNDP played a significant role in the **social reform movements of Kerala**, advocating for the eradication of caste discrimination and promoting the idea of "One Caste, One Religion, One God."
 
• The SNDP Yogam contributed to the **educational and economic empowerment** of the Ezhava community by establishing schools, colleges, and other institutions.
 
• The organization's influence was instrumental in shaping the **progressive social landscape of modern Kerala**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sree Narayana Guru**:

 
 
• Sree Narayana Guru was a **philosopher, spiritual leader, and social reformer** from Kerala, revered for his efforts to fight caste discrimination.
 
• He is best known for his message of universal brotherhood and his teaching of "**One Caste, One Religion, One God for Humanity**."
 
• He consecrated temples that were open to all, breaking traditional caste barriers in worship.
 
 
 
• **Social Reform Movements in Kerala**:
 
 
• Kerala witnessed various social reform movements in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, focusing on **abolishing caste discrimination** and promoting education.
 
• Prominent movements include the **SNDP movement**, the efforts of Chattampi Swamikal, and the Vaikom Satyagraha.
 
 
 
• **Ezhava Community**:
 
 
• The Ezhavas are a prominent community in Kerala who were historically marginalized due to caste-based discrimination.
 
• They benefitted greatly from the social reforms spearheaded by Sree Narayana Guru and the SNDP Yogam.
 
 
 
• **SNDP's Contributions**:
 
 
• The SNDP Yogam established various institutions like **schools, colleges, and cooperative societies** to improve the socio-economic status of the Ezhava community.
 
• It also played a role in Kerala's political and cultural awakening during the early 20th century.

questions.question: Who among the following became the Chairperson of the Parliamentary Committee on Science and Technology, Environment, Forests and Climate Change as on 30th September 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jairam Ramesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jairam Ramesh was appointed as the Chairperson of the Parliamentary Committee on Science and Technology, Environment, Forests, and Climate Change on **30th September 2023**.
 
• He is a senior member of the Indian National Congress (INC) and has been actively involved in policymaking related to environmental and climate issues.
 
• Jairam Ramesh previously served as the Minister of State for Environment and Forests (Independent Charge) from 2009 to 2011, where he introduced several key environmental policies.
 
• His appointment aims to strengthen parliamentary oversight and policy discussions in the domains of science, technology, and environmental sustainability.
 
• The Parliamentary Committee plays a crucial role in reviewing legislation, programs, and policies related to environmental protection, climate change mitigation, and technological advancements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliamentary Committees:**

 
 
• Parliamentary Committees are formed to scrutinize and evaluate specific policies, programs, and bills to ensure accountability and transparency in governance.
 
• They consist of members from both houses of Parliament—Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
 
• Committees like the one on Science and Technology, Environment, Forests, and Climate Change focus on specialized areas requiring in-depth knowledge and deliberation.
 
 
 
• **Climate Change Policy in India:**
 
 
• India has taken significant steps to combat climate change, including its commitment to the Paris Agreement and Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).
 
• Programs like the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) are aimed at promoting sustainable development and reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
 
 
 
• **Science and Technology Initiatives:**
 
 
• India actively promotes research and innovation through organizations like the Department of Science and Technology (DST) and the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).
 
• Advancements in technology are crucial for addressing environmental challenges, including renewable energy and waste management solutions.
 
 
 
• **Role of Parliamentary Oversight:**
 
 
• Parliamentary Committees ensure that government policies align with national priorities and global standards.
 
• They provide recommendations for improvements and help in addressing gaps in policy implementation.

questions.question: The ‘Servants of India Society’ was founded by which of the following freedom fighters?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gopal Krishna Gokhale**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Servants of India Society was founded by **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** on **June 12, 1905** in Pune, Maharashtra.
 
• The primary aim of the society was to train individuals for public service and to promote social and political reforms in India.
 
• Gokhale envisioned the society as a group of selfless workers who would dedicate their lives to the betterment of the country and its people.
 
• The society emphasized education, healthcare, and the upliftment of the underprivileged as core areas of focus.
 
• It played a significant role in fostering the spirit of nationalism and preparing young Indians to contribute to the Indian freedom movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale:**

 
 
• He was a senior leader of the Indian National Congress and a mentor to Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• He advocated for moderate reforms and emphasized constitutional methods for achieving self-rule.
 
 
 
• **Servants of India Society Objectives:**
 
 
• Promotion of education, especially among marginalized sections of society.
 
• Upliftment of the poor and eradication of social evils like untouchability and caste discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Prominent Members:**
 
 
• Key members of the society included Srinivasa Shastri and Dattatraya Balkrishna Kalelkar, who furthered its goals.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• The society's work laid the groundwork for broader social and political reforms in India, influencing future leaders of the independence movement.

questions.question: Which of the following is the quality of the public goods?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-rivalrous**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Public goods** are characterized as **non-rivalrous**, meaning that the consumption of the good by one person does not reduce its availability for others (e.g., national defense, street lighting).
 
• Non-rivalry ensures that no matter how many people use the good, its supply remains unaffected for others.
 
• Examples of non-rivalrous goods include public parks, clean air, and national security.
 
• Public goods are often provided by governments because private markets may fail to offer them due to their non-rivalrous and non-excludable nature.
 
• Non-rivalry is a key component in distinguishing public goods from private goods, which are rivalrous in consumption.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Excludable vs Non-excludable:**

 
 
• **Excludable goods** are those where it is possible to prevent someone from using them (e.g., private goods like a meal in a restaurant).
 
• **Non-excludable goods**, such as public goods, are accessible to everyone (e.g., national defense).
 
 
 
• **Rivalrous vs Non-rivalrous:**
 
 
• **Rivalrous goods** are those that can only be consumed by one person at a time (e.g., a sandwich).
 
• **Non-rivalrous goods** can be consumed by many people simultaneously without depletion (e.g., a lighthouse's signal).
 
 
 
• **Free Rider Problem:**
 
 
• The free rider problem arises with public goods because people can benefit from them without contributing to their cost.
 
• This often leads to under-provision of such goods in a free market, necessitating government intervention.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Public Goods:**
 
 
• Examples include clean air, national defense, public broadcasting, and street lighting.
 
• These goods are typically funded through taxation to ensure universal access.

questions.question: According to the Indian calendar, the March and April months are known as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chaitra-Vaisakha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the Indian calendar, the months of March and April correspond to **Chaitra and Vaisakha**.
 
• The Indian calendar, also known as the **Hindu lunar calendar**, is widely used for determining religious festivals and auspicious days.
 
• Chaitra is the **first month** of the Hindu lunar calendar, marking the beginning of the new year in several Indian traditions.
 
• Vaisakha follows Chaitra and is considered the **second month** in the traditional calendar.
 
• Important festivals such as **Ugadi** (Telugu and Kannada New Year) and **Gudi Padwa** (Marathi New Year) are celebrated during the Chaitra month.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindu Lunar Calendar:**

 
 
• The Hindu calendar is a **lunisolar calendar**, meaning it accounts for both the phases of the moon and the position of the sun.
 
• It consists of **12 months**, each divided into two fortnights: Shukla Paksha (waxing phase) and Krishna Paksha (waning phase).
 
 
 
• **Chaitra Month:**
 
 
• Chaitra marks the beginning of the spring season and is associated with new beginnings in Indian culture.
 
• It is considered an auspicious time for starting new ventures or religious observances.
 
 
 
• **Vaisakha Month:**
 
 
• Vaisakha is associated with the harvest season and is celebrated in various parts of India with festivals like **Baisakhi** in Punjab.
 
• It also marks the birth anniversary of **Lord Buddha**, celebrated as Buddha Purnima.
 
 
 
• **Regional Variations:**
 
 
• The Indian calendar follows different systems regionally, such as the **Vikram Samvat** and **Saka Samvat**.
 
• Despite regional differences, Chaitra and Vaisakha are common months across most systems.

questions.question: Which of the following is the legislative organ of the Union Government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Parliament** is the legislative organ of the Union Government in India.
 
• It consists of two houses: the **Lok Sabha (House of the People)** and the **Rajya Sabha (Council of States)**, along with the President of India.
 
• The primary function of the Parliament is to **frame laws for the country** and amend existing laws as required.
 
• It also oversees the **executive branch**, ensuring accountability through debates, discussions, and the questioning of ministers.
 
• Key legislative powers include passing budgets, enacting laws, and addressing issues of national importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Sabha:**

 
 
• It is the lower house of Parliament and represents the people of India directly.
 
• Members are directly elected by citizens through general elections, held every five years.
 
• The Lok Sabha is responsible for introducing and passing money bills.
 
 
 
• **Rajya Sabha:**
 
 
• It is the upper house of Parliament and represents the states and union territories of India.
 
• Members are elected by the legislative assemblies of states and union territories, and some are nominated by the President for their expertise.
 
• The Rajya Sabha reviews and suggests amendments to bills passed by the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Powers of Parliament:**
 
 
• The Parliament holds the authority to make laws on subjects listed in the Union List, Concurrent List, and, in certain cases, the State List.
 
• In cases of national emergencies, the Parliament gains greater legislative powers over state matters.
 
 
 
• **President's Role:**
 
 
• The President of India is an integral part of the Parliament and is responsible for giving assent to bills passed by both houses before they become laws.
 
• The President can also summon, prorogue, or dissolve the Lok Sabha.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about the Sangeet Natak Akademi is/are true?

1. The Sangeet Natak Akademi has been functioning as the apex body of the performing arts in the country.

2. The main objective of the Akademi is to coordinate and collaborate with the government and performing artists.

3. The Sangeet Natak Akademi comes under the Ministry of Culture of the government of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2, and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Sangeet Natak Akademi** functions as the **apex body for performing arts** in India, promoting and preserving music, dance, and drama.
 
• Established in **1953**, the Akademi operates under the **Ministry of Culture**, Government of India.
 
• The primary objective of the Akademi is to **coordinate and collaborate** with the government, artists, and institutions to promote performing arts.
 
• The Akademi supports individual artists and institutions through awards, fellowships, and grants to preserve India's cultural heritage.
 
• It also works to document and archive rare art forms, ensuring their survival for future generations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards:**

 
 
• The Akademi annually confers awards to individuals for their outstanding contribution to performing arts in India.
 
• These awards recognize achievements in music, dance, theatre, puppetry, and other traditional art forms.
 
 
 
• **Role of Ministry of Culture:**
 
 
• The Ministry of Culture provides funding and policy support to the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
 
• It ensures the Akademi aligns with national initiatives for cultural preservation and promotion.
 
 
 
• **Documentation and Archiving:**
 
 
• The Akademi maintains a vast repository of recordings, manuscripts, and photographs of traditional art forms.
 
• It also publishes books, journals, and research materials to spread awareness about India's cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Other Cultural Institutions under the Ministry:**
 
 
• Similar institutions like the Lalit Kala Akademi (visual arts) and Sahitya Akademi (literature) function under the Ministry of Culture.
 
• These organizations collectively contribute to the preservation and promotion of India's diverse cultural landscape.

questions.question: Which of the following are building blocks of proteins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amino acids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Amino acids** are organic compounds that serve as the building blocks of proteins in living organisms.
 
• Proteins are formed through the polymerization of amino acids via **peptide bonds**, creating long chains known as polypeptides.
 
• There are **20 standard amino acids** commonly found in proteins, which include essential and non-essential amino acids.
 
• **Essential amino acids** cannot be synthesized by the body and must be obtained through diet, whereas non-essential amino acids can be produced internally.
 
• Amino acids play crucial roles in various biological functions, including enzyme activity, cellular structure, and metabolic processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peptide Bond**: A chemical bond formed between two amino acids when the carboxyl group of one reacts with the amino group of another, releasing a molecule of water.
 
• **Protein Structure Levels**: Proteins have four structural levels—primary (sequence of amino acids), secondary (alpha-helices and beta-sheets), tertiary (three-dimensional structure), and quaternary (arrangement of multiple polypeptides).
 
• **Role of Proteins**: Proteins function as enzymes, hormones, antibodies, transport molecules, and structural components in cells and tissues.
 
• **Metabolic Pathways**: Amino acids are precursors for important biomolecules like neurotransmitters, nucleotides, and nitrogen-containing compounds.
 
• **Protein Synthesis**: The process involves transcription (DNA to mRNA) and translation (mRNA to protein), utilizing ribosomes and tRNA for the assembly of amino acids.

questions.question: Which of the following is a NOT a feature of the Indian Parliamentary form of Government?

options.text: Non membership of the ministers in Legislature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-membership of the ministers in Legislature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Parliamentary system follows the principle of **fusion of powers**, where the executive (Prime Minister and Council of Ministers) is part of the legislature.
 
• Ministers must be members of the legislature (either Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha) or must get elected/nominated within six months if not already a member.
 
• The provision of ministers being non-members of the legislature is not in line with the Parliamentary system, as it is a feature of the **Presidential system** like that of the USA.
 
• The Parliamentary system is characterized by the **collective responsibility** of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha, which requires them to be accountable as members of the legislature.
 
• This ensures effective coordination between the legislature and executive, a hallmark of the Indian Parliamentary democracy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliamentary vs Presidential System:**

 
 
• In the Parliamentary system, there is a fusion of powers, whereas in the Presidential system, there is a strict separation of powers.
 
• In the Presidential system, ministers are not part of the legislature, unlike in the Parliamentary system.
 
 
 
• **Collective Responsibility:**
 
 
• The Council of Ministers in India operates on the principle of collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha.
 
• This means that if the government loses confidence in the Lok Sabha, all ministers must resign.
 
 
 
• **Majority Party Rule:**
 
 
• The party or coalition with the majority in the Lok Sabha forms the government in the Indian Parliamentary system.
 
• This ensures stability and reflects the will of the electorate.
 
 
 
• **Dissolution of the Lower House:**
 
 
• The Lok Sabha can be dissolved by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister, marking the end of its term.
 
• This feature allows for fresh elections and the opportunity for the electorate to choose their representatives again.

questions.question: What is the process of a substance changing directly from a solid to a gas without passing through the liquid state called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sublimation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sublimation** is the process where a substance changes directly from a solid to a gas without passing through the liquid state.
 
• Common examples include the sublimation of **dry ice (solid carbon dioxide)** and **naphthalene balls**.
 
• This process occurs when the pressure and temperature conditions are such that the liquid state is bypassed entirely.
 
• Sublimation is commonly observed in substances with strong intermolecular forces and low vapor pressures at room temperature.
 
• The reverse process of a gas turning directly into a solid is also called sublimation or sometimes deposition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Terminology:**

 
 
• **Fusion:** The process of a solid changing into a liquid.
 
• **Evaporation:** The process of a liquid changing into a gas below its boiling point.
 
• **Condensation:** The process of a gas turning into a liquid.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Sublimation:**
 
 
• Sublimation is used in the purification of substances where impurities do not sublimate.
 
• It is used in freeze-drying techniques for preserving perishable materials.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Sublimable Substances:**
 
 
• Dry ice (solid CO₂) changes directly into carbon dioxide gas.
 
• Iodine, camphor, and ammonium chloride are other common examples of substances that sublimate.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Explanation:**
 
 
• The process occurs under specific temperature and pressure conditions where the substance's triple point is bypassed.
 
• At these conditions, the solid's vapor pressure equals the surrounding pressure, leading to direct conversion to the gaseous state.

questions.question: Which type of coal is found in Damodar valley?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bituminous**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bituminous coal** is the most abundant type of coal found in India and is widely used for industrial purposes.
 
• The Damodar Valley, located in eastern India, is one of the richest coal-bearing regions and primarily contains **bituminous coal deposits**.
 
• The coal in this region is known for its high carbon content and **moderate moisture levels**, making it ideal for thermal power generation and steel production.
 
• The Damodar Valley includes major coalfields such as Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro, and Giridih, which are key contributors to India's coal reserves.
 
• Bituminous coal from the Damodar Valley is also utilized in the production of coke, which is essential for metallurgical processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coal Types and Classification:**

 
 
• Coal is classified into four main types: **Anthracite, Bituminous, Lignite, and Peat**, based on carbon content and energy output.
 
• **Anthracite** is the highest grade of coal with the highest carbon content and energy efficiency.
 
• **Lignite** is a lower-grade coal with higher moisture content and lower energy efficiency.
 
• **Peat** is the earliest stage of coal formation, with the lowest carbon content and energy output.
 
 
 
• **Coalfields in India:**
 
 
• India's major coalfields are located in states like Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The Jharia coalfield in Jharkhand is known for its high-grade coking coal used in steel production.
 
• The Raniganj coalfield in West Bengal is one of the oldest coalfields in India.
 
 
 
• **Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC):**
 
 
• DVC was established in 1948 to manage the resources of the Damodar Valley, including coal and water.
 
• It plays a key role in power generation, irrigation, and flood control in the region.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Coal in India:**
 
 
• Coal is a major source of energy in India, contributing to over 50% of the country's electricity generation.
 
• India is the second-largest coal producer in the world, with significant reserves in the eastern and central regions.
 
• The coal industry is vital for industrial growth, particularly in sectors like steel, cement, and thermal power.

questions.question: What is the total length of 'Atal Tunnel', which is located in Himachal Pradesh state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**9.02 kilometres**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Atal Tunnel**, located in Himachal Pradesh, is one of the world's longest highway tunnels at a high altitude, measuring **9.02 kilometres**.
 
• It connects **Manali to Lahaul-Spiti valley** throughout the year, bypassing the Rohtang Pass.
 
• Atal Tunnel was **inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi** on **3 October 2020**.
 
• The tunnel is built at an altitude of **3,000 meters (10,000 feet)** above sea level.
 
• It reduces travel time by about **4 to 5 hours**, ensuring all-weather connectivity and boosting tourism and trade in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Strategic Importance:** The Atal Tunnel enhances military logistics and connectivity to remote areas near the India-China border.
 
• **Engineering Marvel:** The tunnel is equipped with advanced features such as fire hydrants, air monitoring systems, and emergency exits at regular intervals.
 
• **Cost and Construction:** The construction of the tunnel was undertaken by the **Border Roads Organisation (BRO)** at a cost of approximately **₹3,200 crores**.
 
• **Geological Challenges:** The tunnel's construction involved dealing with harsh weather, difficult terrain, and complex geological conditions.
 
• **Tourism Boost:** The Atal Tunnel has emerged as a major tourist attraction, contributing to the economic development of the region.
